newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Blue-chips pull Morocco's bourse down 1.84 pct.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chips pull Morocco's bourse down 1.84 pct.

text.p: Morocco's stock exchange started the week on Monday 1.84 percent lower as biggest holdings Societe Nationale d'Investissement and ONA Group fell in value, stockbrokers said.
The Casablanca bourse all-share index closed at 630.20 from 642.03 points on Thursday.
The bourse was closed on Friday due to a public holiday.
Oil refinery Samir which was increased steadily since its hard core was sold to Swedish-based Saudi Corral group, fell 9.80 dirhams to close at 390 dirhams.
ONA, Morocco's largest private conglomerate, dipped 22 dirhams to 740 dirhams.
SNI, the country's second largest private group also dropped 21 dirhams to 699 dirhams.
In the banking sector, Banque Commerciale du Maroc and Banque Marocaine du Commerce Exterieur lost 23 and 17 dirhams to respectively 754 and 578 dirhams.
Credit firms were also subject to falls, Financiere Diwan dropped 21 dirhams to 353 dirhams.
Morocco has opened on Monday subscriptions on Casablanca bourse for sale of 6.07 percent stake of U.S. businessman George Soros in Financiere Diwan, a broker at ABN-AMRO Finance said.
Total stake floated on the bourse on Monday is estimated at $17.6 million, the broker said.
Soros initially owned nearly 13 percent stake in Diwan whose majority stake is held by ONA.
The closing date for subscription was set for May 30, 1997, a bourse official said.
Eqdom Credit lost 29 dirhams to 967 dirhams.
Credor with minus 22 dirhams to 725 dirhams. Maroc leasing shed 14 dirhams to 455 dirhams.
Total traded volume on the official market was 23.6 million dirhams. On the over-the-counter market, the volume was 13 million dirhams.
